content: Cefpodoxime proxetil is an orally administered, extended-spectrum, semi-synthetic antibiotic that belongs to the cephalosporin class. Its chemical name is (RS)-1-(isopropoxycarbonyloxy) ethyl (+)-(6R,7R)-7-[2-(2-amino-4-thiazolyl)-2-(methoxyimino)acetamido]-3-methoxymethyl-8-oxo-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylate. The empirical formula of cefpodoxime proxetil is C21H27N5O9S2, and its molecular weight is 557.6. Cefpodoxime proxetil is a prodrug, meaning it is converted into its active metabolite, cefpodoxime, after administration. All dosages of cefpodoxime proxetil mentioned in this document are expressed in terms of the active cefpodoxime moiety. The drug is available in two forms: film-coated tablets and flavored granules for oral suspension. VANTIN tablets contain cefpodoxime proxetil equivalent to either 100 mg or 200 mg of cefpodoxime activity. The inactive ingredients in the tablets include carboxymethylcellulose calcium, carnauba wax, FD&C Yellow No. 6, hydroxypropyl cellulose, hypromellose, lactose hydrous, magnesium stearate, propylene glycol, sodium lauryl sulfate, and titanium dioxide. Additionally, the 100 mg tablets contain D&C Yellow No. 10, while the 200 mg tablets contain FD&C Red No. 40. Each 5 mL of VANTIN oral suspension, after reconstitution, contains cefpodoxime proxetil equivalent to either 50 mg or 100 mg of cefpodoxime activity. The inactive ingredients in the oral suspension include artificial flavorings, butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), carboxymethylcellulose sodium, microcrystalline cellulose, carrageenan, citric acid, colloidal silicon dioxide, croscarmellose sodium, hydroxypropyl cellulose, lactose, maltodextrin, natural flavorings, propylene glycol alginate, sodium citrate, sodium benzoate, starch, sucrose, and vegetable oil.
